question: What will be US initial jobless claims for the week (seasonally adjusted, Department of Labor) for the week ending 2026-08-29, as first published?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the first published value of US initial jobless claims for the week (seasonally adjusted, Department of Labor) for the week ending 2026-08-29 (FRED series ICSA). Later revisions are ignored.
research:
Page fetches are failing, so I'm writing this up from the search results I already have.

## 1. Resolution source
- The deciding figure is the seasonally adjusted initial claims number for the week ending 2026-08-29, as first published in DOL's weekly release (FRED series ICSA). That release should come out Thursday 2026-09-03 at 8:30 ET. I could not open FRED or the DOL release directly because the proxy refused the connection. [FRED ICSA](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/ICSA)
- 2026-08-20: The latest print available before the cutoff is 206,000 for the week ending Aug 15. That was down 6,000 from the prior week, which was revised up to 212,000 from 209,000. Consensus had been about 210,000. [investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/us-initial-jobless-claims-206k-vs-210k-expected/), [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/articles/u-weekly-jobless-claims-fall-124023010.html)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The week being measured has not started, and the number comes out about two weeks after the forecast closes.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-20: Week ending Aug 15 came in at 206K, against roughly 210K expected. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/articles/u-weekly-jobless-claims-fall-124023010.html)
- 2026-08-13: Week ending Aug 8 first printed at 209K, up 9K. It was later revised to 212K. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/articles/u-weekly-jobless-claims-rose-123847527.html)
- 2026-08-06: Week ending Aug 1 was 199K, which a secondary source described as "near cycle lows." Continuing claims "jumped." [VerifiedInvesting](https://verifiedinvesting.com/blogs/us-economic-metrics/jobless-claims-week-ending-august-1-2026)
- 2026-07-30: Week ending Jul 25 was 197K, up 9K, against a 200K estimate. Continuing claims were 1.782M. [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/bgov-labor/us-weekly-jobless-claims-rise-9k-to-197k-est-200k)
- 2026-07-23: Week ending Jul 18 was 187K, down 22K. The 4-week average was 207,500. [trade.gov.tr](https://trade.gov.tr/news/us-weekly-initial-claims-was-187-000)
- July 2026: Week ending Jul 11 was 208K (4-week average 214,250). Week ending Jul 4 was 215K, against 217K expected (4-week average 218,750). [trade.gov.tr](https://trade.gov.tr/news/us-weekly-initial-claims-was-208-000), [trade.gov.tr](https://trade.gov.tr/news/the-us-weekly-initial-claims-was-215-000), [Staffing Industry](https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/weekly-jobless-claims-edge-down-beating-economist-forecasts)

## 4. Base rates
- First prints over the last seven weeks: 215K, 208K, 187K, 197K, 199K, 209K, 206K. That is a range of 187K to 215K, with a mean of about 203K and a median of 206K.
- Changes from one week to the next are usually a few thousand to about 10K. The largest move in this run was -22K (Jul 18). Over the two-week gap between the latest print and the target week, a move of about ±10 to 15K is typical. Moves above 20K happen occasionally.
- The trend has drifted down since early July: the 4-week average fell from about 219K to roughly 205 to 207K. Revisions are usually small, about +0 to 3K (for example, 209K was revised to 212K).
- Kalshi had spring 2026 contracts with strikes between 165K and 185K for the week of May 7. That suggests claims were even lower in spring. [simplefunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/api/public/market/KXJOBLESSCLAIMS-26MAY07-185000)
- Seasonal comparison, from my memory and not verified: the matching late-August weeks first printed at about 237K in 2025 (week ending Aug 30) and about 227K in 2024 (week ending Aug 31). Both years were at a higher overall level than 2026. Labor Day 2026 falls on Sept 7, so the holiday should not distort the target week.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi lists a market for this week (KXJOBLESSCLAIMS-26SEP03), but the snapshot I found says it only opens 2026-08-27. That is after the cutoff, so I could not see any price before the cutoff. [bitcoin.com mirror](https://www.bitcoin.com/prediction-markets/kalshi/initial-jobless-claims-for-the-week-ending-august-29-2026--KXJOBLESSCLAIMS-26SEP03/)
- For comparison, Kalshi's market for the week ending Aug 1 was priced at about 62% for 205K or more, 47% for 210K or more, and 23% for 215K or more. The actual first print was 199K. [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxjoblessclaims/weekly-initial-jobless-claims/kxjoblessclaims-26aug06)
- I found no Polymarket or Manifold market and no published consensus for this specific week. Recent consensus has sat around 208K to 210K.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-08-27: Claims for the week ending Aug 22 are released, along with revisions to the Aug 15 week. This is the last print before the target and the main new information.
- Early September: the August jobs report (normally the first Friday, possibly 2026-09-04, after this resolves) plus any news of layoffs or company announcements.
- Things that can push a single week around: hurricane-season storms (late August is peak season), state-level filing anomalies, and seasonal-factor quirks around the end of summer and the return to school.
